newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania revises deficit, inflation forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Romania revises deficit, inflation forecasts.

text.p: Romania's outgoing government on Tuesday revised upward forecasts for the 1996 budget deficit and inflation well beyond levels agreed with the International Monetary Fund.

Figures announced by Finance Minister Florin Georgescu showed the leftist government, voted out of office this month, leaving economic difficulties for its centrist coalition successor worse than had been anticipated.

Georgescu predicted a consolidated budget deficit of 4.0 percent of gross domestic product, compared to original forecasts of 2.2 percent as agreed with the IMF and later adjusted to 3.0 percent. He forecast a 1997 deficit of 3.7 percent.
Growth in GDP was forecast at 4.8 percent, up from recent estimates of 4.5 percent. The 1997 forecast was 5.5 percent.
Inflation for 1996 was forecast at 38 percent against original plans for 20 percent, also readjusted later to 30 percent. It was put at 25 percent for 1997.
The trade deficit for 1997 was forecast at $200 million. Figures so far for this year put the deficit at $589 million from January-September.
Georgescu declined to say at which exchange rate for the leu currency he had made the calculations.
The new centrist is committed to a programme of faster reforms and tax cuts and is likely to overhaul all the figures.
Georgescu blamed the increased deficit on allocations to farmers affected by bad weather and higher expenditure to supplement benefits to hard-hit consumers in an election year.
"The deficit of the consolidated budget estimated at 4.0 or 4.1 percent of the GDP is consistent with conditions in this electoral year," he said.
"Neither the deficit nor the budget itself is created by an individual but by a society with demands. We gave in to pressure from social groups to index salaries."
He said the 1996 GDP would reach 111.6 trillion lei, in line with recent forecasts. This was due to rise to 154.8 trillion next year.
The new estimate would put the deficit at 4.46 trillion lei. Earlier figures had suggested a deficit of 4.27 trillion for the end of the year.

The IMF suspended loan tranches for Romania this year after expressing concern over foreign exchange market restrictions and lax budgetary discipline ahead of the election. ($=3,502 lei) -- Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
